For recycling, the separated NUC-155a was washed twice with dichloromethane (DCM), dried under vacuum, and reused in subsequent runs. 2.5.Catalyst activation and general procedure General procedure: Prior to catalysis, NUC-155 was activated in two steps: (i) solvent exchange of the as-synthe‐ sized crystals with methanol (72 h), and (ii) vacuum drying (12 h) to remove methanol and coordinated DMF, afford‐ ing NUC-155a. Cycloaddition reactions were performed (solvent- free unless noted) in a PTFE-lined autoclave charged with the epoxide and NUC-155a and connected to a CO2 cylinder via a pressure regulator. 2-(Trifluorometh‐ yl)oxirane (TFO) served as the model substrate for condition optimization; thereafter, epoxides bearing electron- withdrawing, electron-donating, and sterically demanding substituents were examined to assess substrate scope. Af‐ ter reaction, the mixture was diluted with ethyl acetate, and the heterogeneous catalyst was recovered by centrifuga‐ tion. For recycling, the separated NUC-155a was washed twice with dichloromethane (DCM), dried under vacuum, and reused in subsequent runs.
